title: Go-to-Prod Rapid Response Ops Logbook
body:
Purpose
This document is a compact, tactical playbook and logbook for product ops to run a rapid-response go-to-production window. It combines a focused roadmap tracker, the KPI pack we will monitor during the ramp, and the launch readiness checklist used for go/no-go and early escalation.

Scope and assumptions
- Scope: initial public ramp for a latency-sensitive hosted API feature (streaming endpoints, new routing policy).
- Assumes Dedicated capacity warmup completed 48h prior, model variants smoke-tested, and infra runbooks applied to stage and prod clusters.
- Objective: reach steady-state 95% of baseline throughput within 72h without regressions to median latency or cost-per-token beyond defined thresholds.

How to use this logbook
- Pre-launch: use sections A+B to verify readiness and owners.
- Launch window: update the KPI snapshot every 30 minutes in the Ops Warboard. Document anomalies here with timestamps.
- Post-mortem: move entries to the postlaunch section and tag contributors.

A. Minimum acceptance KPIs (live tracking items)
- Latency (p50/p95/p99): target p50 <= 220ms, p95 <= 420ms, p99 <= 900ms. Alert if p95 exceeds target by 30% for >10m.
- Error rate (5m rolling): target <0.5% client errors, <0.1% server 5xx. Alert at 1% client errors or any sustained 5xx > 0.2%.
- Throughput: target sustained QPS per shard within 10% of predicted capacity. Alert if realized throughput <75% of expected for >15m.
- Cost per 1k tokens: baseline measured during canary. Flag +20% cost delta and investigate batch sizes/quant profiles.
- Quality regressions: automatic eval set (50 prompts) should have no more than 5% degradation in BLEU/ROUGE-style metric and manual review of 10 samples.

B. Early warning signals (EWS) and thresholds
- Queue depth > 60s median latency to dequeue.
- Model fallback rate > 2% (routing to cheaper variants indicates capacity pressure).
- Cache hit rate drop > 15% (prefix cache flushing).
- Elevated KV cache misses correlated with p95 jumps.
- Operator notes: if multiple EWS fire within 10m, trigger Level 2 ops (see Runbook).

C. Roles and contact quickmap (on-call first, then escalation)
- Launch Lead (single point decision): Leah Moroz (owner) — call sign: "Launch Lead".
- Runtime SME: Diego Alvarez — responsible for batching and runtime kernel toggles.
- Model/Quality SME: Juniper Li — run eval set, approve rollbacks for model variants.
- Capacity & Scaling: Nora Patel — dedicated capacity shifts and autoscale policies.
- SRE Pager: SRE team oncall (team channel: #sre-launch).
- Customer comms: Maria Gomez (CS) if customers impacted.

D. Go/No-go checklist (2 hours before window and immediate pre-traffic)
Pre-2h must-haves:
- Canary run results: all KPIs green for 2h in canary (p95 within 10% of baseline).
- Infra flags set: routing policy toggles validated and feature flags staged.
- Observability: dashboards wired, alert thresholds agreed in the Ops Warboard.
- Runbooks: quick rollback and capacity bump steps validated by SRE.
- Stakeholder alignment: product, eng, SRE, and CS listed in Slack huddle.

Immediate pre-traffic (T-10m):
- CD pipeline: deployment green, artifacts verified.
- DB/Cache warms: data migrations complete or confirmed not required.
- Throttle parameters: default throttle set and can be adjusted without deploy.
- Escalation list present in warboard with phone numbers and secondary contacts.

E. Rapid response runbook (leveled)
Level 1: operator fix (Launch Lead or Runtime SME)
- Symptoms: small p95 bump, single-service error spike.
- Actions: clear slow queues, adjust batch window by -10ms, restart single worker pool. Log start/stop times here.

Level 2: cross-team action (SRE + Runtime + Model SME)
- Symptoms: sustained p95 > threshold, model fallback rate increasing, cache hit collapse.
- Actions: divert X% traffic to fallback region (policy), increase Dedicated shard by +1 for 30m, toggle conservative kernel path, run partial rollback to prev model variant. Notify Launch Lead.

Level 3: emergency rollback / preserve customers
- Symptoms: customer impact, data loss risks, or cascading 5xx.
- Actions: full rollback to last known-good deployment, announce to customers through CS, open incident and assign Incident Commander.

F. Tactical timeline template (sample)
- T-48h: Warm dedicated pools, run 6h synthetic load tests.
- T-24h: Final smoke tests, preflight KPI snapshot.
- T-6h: Ops warboard up, alert thresholds set, quick huddle with stakeholders.
- T-2h: Execute pre-2h checklist.
- T-10m: verify pre-traffic items, lift traffic gating.
- T+0: inject 5% traffic for 20m then 25% for 40m then 50% — monitor KPIs and decide cadence.
- T+72h: expected steady-state and signoff for feature flag expansion to 100%.

G. Lightweight roadmap tracker (what to log during ramp)
- Item: Rolling throughput vs expected — log timestamps and owner notes.
- Item: Latency deviations and correlated infra changes.
- Item: Cache hit rate and KV miss explosions.
- Item: Model eval drift instances and manual review links.
- Item: Cost delta events and mitigation steps taken.

H. Quick templates for entries (paste into warboard)
- [HH:MM UTC] KPI ALERT: p95 620ms (target 420ms) — owner: Diego — action: increased shard, toggled kernel path, p95 fell to 430ms after 12m.
- [HH:MM UTC] QUALITY CHECK: eval set drift 7% — owner: Juniper — action: paused rollout to 25% and queued manual sample review.

I. Post-launch cool-down & artifacts to produce
- 24h: launch summary note with KPI delta and top 3 mitigations.
- 72h: readiness signoff doc with final pass/fail on launch SLOs.
- 7 days: retrospective with action items and roadmap updates (owners assigned).

Appendix: Quick links and commands
- Warboard dashboard: (CONFLUENCE-12345)
- Ops runbook commands: 
  - scale-up shard: /ops scale shards --region us-west2 --add 1
  - rollback deploy: /deploy rollback --to-tag stable-20251104

Notes and open questions
- Can we pre-populate the eval sample set with flagged user prompts to validate hallucination regressions? (Juniper follow-up)
- Confirm SLA wording for Dedicated customers if we triage traffic to fallback variants. (Nora action)

Sign-off
- Leah Moroz (Launch Lead) — draft v0.9
- Diego Alvarez (Runtime SME) — reviewed
